newsitem.title: SUDAN: IMF in Sudan for talks including arrears, deficit.
newsitem.headline: IMF in Sudan for talks including arrears, deficit.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) team is in Sudan for talks on the impoverished country's economy, debts and budget deficit, a state-run newspaper said on Tuesday.
Al-Ingaz al-Watani said officials from both sides would continue discussions on liberalising Sudan's battered currency as well as trade in petroleum products, arrears and other issues.
Sudan owes the IMF over $1.7 billion in arrears. To avoid being expelled, it agreed last year to pay $4 million a month, about enough to cover the interest. But it later failed to honour the pledge.
The IMF urges Sudan to reduce budget deficit by slashing public expenditure, float the currency and remove restrictions on imports by private sector.
On Tuesday residents reported queues at filling stations and a resumption of rationing of petrol.

State governor Majzoub al-Khalifa in remarks published in the daily Independent said there were acute fuel shortages in the country but hoped the crisis to ease with the arrival of new shipments of benzene and other oil products at Port Sudan.
Protests flared earlier this year in Sudan over rising prices, including those for fuel and food.
